motivation: Miyasaka first used metal-halide perovskites as light absorbers in photovoltaic cells (2009). Park made the first stable, efficient solid-state perovskite cell (2012). Snaith showed that perovskites carry charge ambipolarly over long distances, which made thin-film planar devices possible (2012–2013). Together they opened a new class of solution-processable semiconductors. These materials combine sharp absorption edges, low energy disorder, defect tolerance and long carrier diffusion lengths, an unusual set of properties that has changed how we understand electronic and ionic transport in soft, ionic lattices. In just over a decade, single-junction efficiencies rose above 26% and perovskite-silicon tandems passed 33%, beyond the single-junction silicon limit. Commercial production is now starting. Few discoveries in condensed matter physics have moved so quickly from fundamental physics to a technology that could substantially lower the cost of decarbonising the world's electricity supply.
